- **State: CLOUD SECOND FIX ROUND COMPLETE, NOT CLOSED, DO NOT MERGE.**
  - Owner-side second local validation of fix-round head `351de917f7064c6eef0a117a31b3d2579abea671` failed with one unresolved MAJOR class: present but malformed containers were silently dropped. The class was already present in `80b15eb`.
  - It is fixed on `cloud/stage13-open-ended-evolution`. PR #2 is updated, not merged, and no new PR was opened. The canonical `wip/ayas-graphify-final-execution` branch was not touched.

- **Root cause.** The normalizer read containers with truthy/shape coercion (`?? {}`, `Array.isArray(x) ? x : []`, enum defaults), so a present value of the wrong shape read as an absent one. `lifecycle: "REJECTED"` / `["REJECTED"]` / `0` loaded as a fresh OBSERVED record, and a REJECTED opportunity came back as PROPOSAL_READY. Non-array `constraints`, `prerequisites`, `requiredAuthority`, `replacesCapabilities`, `retiresCapabilities` and `evidence` vanished the same way.
- **Fixed. PRESENT + MALFORMED is never ABSENT:**
  - A malformed lifecycle (or one without its state and history), a `null` or non-array carried list, target or register is refused.
  - Every other wrong-shape container, text or closed-vocabulary value (`null` included), and every unknown or misspelled field, is a BLOCKING issue. There are 18 new codes, so the vocabulary is now 61, and `SUPERSEDED_BY_INVALID` is now BLOCKING.
  - A persisted record must carry its carried issues and signals.
  - A BLOCKING record lists every authority class as required; none is granted.
  - Malformed resources or side effects become an explicit UNKNOWN resource or side effect.
  - Directives hidden in malformed shapes are still detected.
  - The register boundary (build and qualify) validates in-memory record shape.
  - The environment facts and the CLI refuse malformed input.
  - A garbled REJECTED record still blocks its revival (DUPLICATE when declarations are unverifiable).
  - An existing-benchmark plan with an unmappable category is NEEDS_INVESTIGATION.
  - No authority was added.
- **Evaluation.**
  - The evaluator was extended with a `container` group, C01–C27, for 54 + 8 + 20 + 27 = **109** (SHA-256 `5acb6303690d099a6c0fafd41c71abd4159973b6069808a38a298192ab31e47b`). Held-out is unchanged, and scenario 52's needles were extended (stricter).
  - `351de917` sources: 54/54, 8/8, 20/20, **container 0/27**. Fixed: 109/109.
  - The bounded shape matrix covers 443 cases. The round-trip, adversarial (32 subsets) and garbled-rejected-revival scenarios pass.
  - Seeded scratch fuzz of 8,883 corrupted records: 0 violations on the fix, and 7,281 on `351de917` (728 reached PROPOSAL_READY).
- **Regressions:**
  - Stage 8 loop: 36 + 55.
  - Stage 7: 41/41 + 5/5.
  - Stage 10: 39/39 flow, 61/61 component, 14/14 integration (the pre-existing held-out miss is unchanged).

## AYAS PC-OFF SAFE RESEARCH — RESTART-SAFE GOAL RESEARCH, LIVENESS-BASED MISSED DETECTION — 2026-09-24

- **Recovery point.** Resumed a Claude/Codex handoff without resetting it. Branch `wip/ayas-graphify-final-execution`; local, upstream and real GitHub origin all `aef70134682a8e2a3d481011d61fb0036a47257b` (ahead/behind 0/0), nothing staged. The worktree held the uncommitted sprint: 17 modified and 3 untracked files, +975/−103. That is exactly the last Claude handoff, so there were no further Codex changes. Graphify was current at `aef7013` and already covered the new files. The work was classified IMPLEMENTED_PARTIALLY_VALIDATED; all of it was kept and completed.
- **Open questions closed first.** Discovery-registry smoke: 14/15. The 15th fails with `0 !== 1` identically on an untouched `git archive aef7013` TEMP copy. Root cause: its fixture repository writes no `.graphify/branch.json`, which the discovery freshness gate (since `4fc5b64`, 2026-09-21) requires. It is PRE_EXISTING, not a regression, and the expectation was not touched. Proposal-approval smoke: 27/27 on TEMP git repos and bare remotes, run to completion.
- **Live safety note.** The running observer spawns `ayas-discovery-daemon.ts` from this worktree every five minutes, so the live daemon executed the in-progress code throughout. Live scheduler state stayed schema-compatible (schema `1`; old readers ignore new optional fields). The one behavior change that would have hit live health — counting a cycle with any flaky feed as a failure, which feeds the stability and health guards — was reverted before the next due LIGHT cycle.
- **Review and fixes** (HIGH `code-review`, three passes: 10, 10 and 9 findings):
  - **MAJOR:** on-time jobs were treated as missed, because any lateness past the exact due instant counted and the heartbeat is five minutes. Replaced by a durable liveness record (`research/scheduler-heartbeat.json`). It is written on every tick before the lock, and its `liveSince` starts a new streak after a gap over 20 minutes, a backwards clock or an unreadable record. A job is missed iff `liveSince > scheduledFor`, so queueing or a long run holding the lock is not downtime, while downtime after an on-time deferral is.
  - **MAJOR:** the flaky-feed cycle failure above, reverted: `consecutiveFailures` again counts only uncertain or thrown cycles.
  - Backlog coalescing is now per Goal, among runnable, missed, unconfirmed catch-ups only.
  - Source pacing may defer a job only inside its policy window; beyond it the policy decides (`PACING_REQUIRES_OWNER` / `PACING_WINDOW_EXCEEDED`), so a far-future check time cannot park a job for days or throw.
  - Decisions are computed inside a fault guard (`GOAL_TICK_FAILED`), and a failed decision write retries on the next heartbeat.
  - A Goal-path fault never stalls the cadence; `lastGoalFaultAt` survives later cycles.
  - The Goal and its job are created together under the lock (`createAndScheduleAyasGoalResearch`); a busy lock or rejected request creates nothing, and a failed job write cancels the new Goal.
  - Capacity pruning is staged and keeps open jobs, recent uncertain outcomes and 24-hour pacing evidence.
  - Explicit completion codes: `INSUFFICIENT_SOURCE_EVIDENCE`, `EVIDENCE_ALREADY_RECORDED`, `RESEARCH_SOURCE_FAILURE` (feed not readable) and `RESEARCH_ANALYSIS_FAILED` (local model or recording).
  - A confirmation clears the stale parking reason.
  - Schedule rules and limits now live in one place in `src/lib`; the Brain action is session check plus service call, and the panel sends only the policy.

## AYAS MEMORY TEMPORAL V2 — CURRENT VS HISTORICAL MEMORY, DERIVED SUPERSESSION — 2026-09-24

- **Recovery point.** Resumed Claude's interrupted Memory Temporal v2 sprint without resetting it. Branch `wip/ayas-graphify-final-execution`; local HEAD, upstream and real GitHub origin all `78daaddca8d1d1686799e75f1b99f63b8aa197f9` (ahead/behind 0/0), nothing staged, `git diff --check` clean, no sprint commit. The previous session left 9 modified and 6 untracked in-scope files (last edit 2026-09-23 23:57). They held a complete temporal core, store/recall/retrieval/chat/trace integration, a 37-scenario smoke suite (numbers 31–37 already carried one review pass), fixtures, a benchmark and a dry-run analyzer. None of it had been validated, and there were no docs, checkpoint entry or commit. Graphify was `stale=false` at `78daadd`, but it had been built at 22:46, before every temporal edit, so it was refreshed with scope `all` before any source reading. Nothing was discarded; all work was completed in place.
- **Contract.** Optional, versioned (`2`), fingerprint-bound `temporal` block with a closed key set: `assertion` (current/historical/future), `provenance` (class only), `recordedAt`, `effectiveFrom`/`effectiveUntil`, `heldFrom`/`heldUntil` (a named period in which the fact held at some point, added this session so "2024'te İzmir'de yaşıyordum" no longer invents a start and end), `effectivePrecision`, and `factKey`/`factValue` (closed registry: identity name, response length, voice length). It sits outside `recordId`, so v1 readers recompute the same identity. Validation rejects reversed or incoherent intervals (a named period or historical start after the statement). Supersession is derived at read time and never stored. Recall modes are current (default), current+history, and as-of `{at, until?, knownAt?}` graded certain/possible; a malformed as-of query selects nothing. Full contract: `docs/AYAS_MEMORY_TEMPORAL.md`.
- **Review.** HIGH `code-review`, four passes: 10, 10, 10 and 10 findings. Each pass's fixes were re-reviewed, because the identity heuristics kept opening new edge cases. The final design principle is that a wrong name is never stored or forced: an unclear statement is *withdrawn*/null, and the chat identity guard stands down. Fixed:
  - per-clause/segment identity reading in v1 pattern order; negated, past-copula, question and conditional names withdrawn; no one-word guessing;
  - "adım" anchored (it is also "step");
  - "beni X olarak"/"bana X diye" only with the positive instruction;
  - each slot's time read from its own segment;
  - historical periods stored as `heldFrom/heldUntil`, with a future-month guard;
  - past-tense detection by the voicing rule plus a loanword list, and present-cue clauses kept current;
  - years need year-shaped context, and product numbers are skipped;
  - the copula after an apostrophe detected;
  - negated length cues (including negative imperatives) state nothing;
  - identity records fill only the identity slot;
  - accents folded, including ø/ł/ß;
  - curly apostrophes normalized in the extractor gate;
  - the chat guard uses the resolver's structured `identityValue`, reads history through the extractor gate plus the writer's rules, never answers a turn that states a name, and stands down when a newer unreadable identity statement exists (selected or quarantined);
  - store: lock-ownership re-check before rename, `writeFileSync(fd)` + `fsyncSync` before rename, guarded temp and lock cleanup, `prune` rejects an unparseable time.

  Kept by design, with rationale in the doc:
  - whole-store fail-closed on an unknown schema;
  - per-record `remove()` restoring the previous version (the v1 contract; no production caller);
  - expired records excluded before resolution — safe because user-stated slots never expire, pinned by smoke 44;
  - one fsync per stored candidate.

  Two edit-tool artifacts caught during the session: a backspace byte in four regexes and a trimmed space in the extractor gate. Both were fixed, and every changed file was scanned for control bytes.
- **Legacy / migration: NONE performed.** Read-only analysis of a TEMP copy of the live `data/brain/memory/records.json` (source SHA-256 unchanged before and after): 28 records, all v1. 22 identity records form 17 versions (1 current, 21 superseded, 0 disputed/conflicting), 22/22 derive exactly v1's value, the current name matches v1's winner, 0 unkeyed identity records, the chat guard keeps a certain name, and 28/28 are readable without migration.

  - The chat route has one turn lifecycle: a `finishTurn` helper, an outer catch for setup throws, and a stream `cancel()` that records `cancelled`. Previously a client abort or disconnect was recorded as `error`, and the report-center branch finished its trace before work that can throw.

  - Only the domain call sits inside each `try`, and `ayasTraceErrorCode` never throws, so a trace call can never replace a domain result or error.

- **Security.** The `security-review` skill could not start: its preamble requires an `origin/HEAD` ref this clone lacks, and git refs were not changed to force it. An equivalent manual review found no vulnerability:
  - Middleware plus route-level auth protect the endpoint.
  - Unauthenticated, tampered, expired, garbage, misconfigured-gate and production-no-key reads all get 401.
  - Another session's trace and malformed, forged or unknown IDs all get the same 404.
  - Responses are `no-store`, and the body carries no prompt, token, scope or key.
  - Metadata is an allowlist; error codes are regex- and secret-word-filtered.
  - Storage is bounded and trace IDs are never an authority token.

## AYAS M25 — SELF-IMPROVEMENT RELIABILITY FORENSICS: OBSERVER AUTOSTART HAD NO CRASH-RESTART SUPERVISION — ROOT-CAUSED, REPAIRED, LIVE-RECOVERY-PROVEN — COMMITTED / PUSHED (`4e3c2f4`) — 2026-09-21

- **Owner report investigated**: no self-improvement activity since M24 (2026-09-18). Confirmed real: `approval-inbox.json` unchanged at 25 proposals (STALE 17 / ABANDONED 1 / COMPLETED 7, zero non-terminal) since M23/M24, no new `micro-items/*.json` since 2026-09-18T18:53, and the research scheduler's own `nextLightAt`/`nextDeepAt` had both lapsed (Sep 18 23:10 and Sep 19 11:07) by the time this sprint started (Sep 21).
- **Full chain traced, per Phase 0's required order, from live state, not assumption.** Scheduler/discovery/proposal/persistence links were all proven healthy; the break is squarely at Autostart → Observer Process:
  1. `data/brain/autonomy/daemon-state.json` showed a heartbeat at `2026-09-21T03:46:30Z` (heartbeatCount 542) — genuinely recent, not stale — yet no `node`/`tsx` observer process was running minutes later (`daemon.lock`'s PID confirmed dead via `Get-Process`).
  2. Correlated with `explorer.exe` (the desktop shell) restarting at `2026-09-21T06:46:14` local — 16s before the observer started — against `(Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem).LastBootUpTime` of **2026-09-15**: this was an interactive **logon**, not a reboot. The observer's only autostart mechanism, a Windows Startup-folder shortcut (`register-ayas-autonomy-autostart.ps1`), fires exclusively on interactive logon — so for however long between the prior session ending and this logon, self-improvement could not have been running at all, by design of that mechanism, not by any code defect in the scheduler itself.
  3. The single tick that did run started an overdue DEEP research cycle (`data/brain/self-improvement/research/scheduler-state.json`: `lastDeepStartedAt` stamped, `lastDeepCompletedAt` still 3 days stale, `currentRunId`/`currentMode: DEEP` left set) and then the **entire process tree vanished within under a minute** of acquiring the research execution-authority lock (owner PID also confirmed dead). No crash log, no stderr — consistent with the whole console/session being closed rather than an in-process exception (the daemon's own `main().catch` reports and exits non-zero on a real exception; this left nothing).
  4. **Nothing was defective in recovery logic itself** — proven, not assumed: `tickAyasResearchScheduler` self-heals a leftover `currentRunId` on its very next tick (by design, `AyasResearchScheduler.ts:85-90`), and `AyasExecutionAuthorityLock`'s 10-minute staleness window (deliberately conservative, to never steal a live owner's lock) is the ONLY reason a manual reclaim attempt 7 minutes after the crash correctly returned `ANOTHER_RUN_ACTIVE` rather than proceeding. A controlled reproduction run **10 minutes after the crash** (`npx tsx scripts/ayas-autonomy-daemon.ts`, single tick) completed a full real DEEP cycle: `researchOutcome: "DEEP"`, `researchFindingsRecorded: 16`, `nextLightAt`/`nextDeepAt` correctly re-anchored to `now + interval` (proves the documented catch-up semantics — one catch-up cycle, never a replay of missed intervals) — this is the Phase-0-required proof of heartbeat recovery, one controlled discovery cycle, and the next cycle remaining scheduled.
  5. **Classification: PARTIALLY_WORKING.** Scheduler/discovery/persistence: fully correct and self-healing. Autostart/process supervision: broken — a Startup-folder shortcut has no crash-restart semantics, so any process death (crash, or the owning console/session ending) silently ends self-improvement until the next interactive logon, which on a personal machine can be days.
- **Smallest safe repair, in two parts, both scoped to autostart/process-supervision only — no scheduler, discovery, proposal, execution, or approval code touched.**
  1. `register-ayas-autonomy-autostart.ps1` / `unregister-ayas-autonomy-autostart.ps1`: now mirror the already-proven pattern this same repo uses for the sibling "AYAS Access Online" daemon (`register-ayas-autostart.ps1`) — Task Scheduler first (`AtLogOn`, current user, `-RunLevel Limited`, no elevation, `-RestartCount 3 -RestartInterval 1min`), falling back to the Startup-folder shortcut only if Task Scheduler registration is refused by the session's own permissions. Unlike the Access daemon (a short idempotent run that exits quickly), the observer is genuinely long-running, so `ExecutionTimeLimit` is explicitly set to `[TimeSpan]::Zero` (indefinite) rather than the module's 3-day default, which would otherwise have killed a healthy `-Continuous` observer outright every 3 days. Both mechanisms now launch with `-WindowStyle Hidden` (plus the shortcut's own minimized `WindowStyle=7` as belt-and-braces) — a visible perpetual console window is a plausible proximate trigger for an unaware user closing it, and this removes that risk regardless of which autostart mechanism is active. Registering via Task Scheduler now also cleans up any leftover shortcut from a prior install, so exactly one mechanism is ever active.
  2. **The mechanism that actually closes the gap, verified in THIS environment**: `Register-ScheduledTask` is itself refused by this session's own permissions (`Erişim engellendi` / HRESULT `0x80070005`) — confirmed both by a direct probe and by the pre-existing sibling "AYAS Access Online" task never having registered via Task Scheduler either (`Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName "AYAS Access Online"` returns nothing; it silently uses the shortcut fallback today). Task Scheduler restart-on-failure therefore cannot be assumed available on every machine/session this project runs under (a `npm run production:acceptance:*`-style silent per-environment gate would be the wrong lesson here — this needed an environment-independent fix). `ayas-autonomy-daemon.ps1` now wraps its own `-Continuous` launch in a bounded restart loop (`-MaxRestarts 10`, `-RestartDelaySeconds 30`, both overridable — production callers never override them): the wrapper (a separate, much simpler PowerShell process unlikely to share the observer's own crash cause) restarts the observer on any non-zero exit, up to 10 times, giving up with a final visible non-zero exit only after that budget is exhausted. An exact `0` exit is trusted as deliberate and never retried — `ayas-autonomy-daemon.ts`'s own continuous loop has no code path that returns 0 while `--continuous` is set, so this can never mask a real, intentional stop.
  3. **Disclosed as a real, currently-active but separate defect, not folded into this fix**: `AyasExecutionAuthorityLock`'s stale-reclaim path (used by the research scheduler) requires the full 10-minute age window before even checking liveness, unlike the observer's own singleton lock (`AyasObserverSingletonLock`, M12), which reclaims a *confirmed-dead* owner immediately regardless of age. Given the restart loop now typically recovers a crashed observer within ~30-60s, a crash mid-research-cycle will still show `ANOTHER_RUN_ACTIVE` for up to ~10 minutes after each recovery before research can resume — correct, not a hang, but slower than it needs to be. Backlog item: give the research lock the same confirmed-dead-immediate-reclaim path the observer lock already has.
  4. **Found and fixed one more, independently confirmed live-impacting defect while exercising the system**: M24 added `data/brain/self-improvement/research-novelty/` (`AyasResearchNoveltyStore`) but never added its `.gitignore` line. The real novelty store was empty until this sprint's own reproduction ran the first genuine production DEEP cycle since M24 — the moment it wrote a real record, `git status --porcelain` went non-empty, which is exactly what the observer's own `repoClean` check reads to decide `OBSERVING` vs `PAUSED_DIRTY_REPO`. Left unfixed, this would have silently reproduced the identical self-improvement outage on the very next otherwise-healthy tick. Fixed with one `.gitignore` line, matching the exact convention of every sibling self-improvement subtree.
- **Tests**: `scripts/smoke-ayas-observer-autostart.ts` grew from 26 to 35 scenarios — Task Scheduler registration/idempotence/dry-run/unregister (environment-tolerant: asserts the Task-Scheduler-specific contract when this session can grant it, the fallback contract otherwise — verified against BOTH outcomes, not assumed), the Task-Scheduler-supersedes-a-leftover-shortcut cleanup, and two real behavioral tests for the new restart loop (a persistently-crashing shim is retried exactly `-MaxRestarts` times then reports failure; a cleanly-exiting shim is never retried). `scripts/smoke-project-storage-hygiene.ts` gained a general regression guard (not just today's one path): every `data/brain/self-improvement/<name>/` subtree actually present on disk must have a matching `.gitignore` rule, so a future sprint that adds another durable subtree and forgets this same line fails CI instead of silently reproducing this outage. All real `Register-ScheduledTask`/`Unregister-ScheduledTask` calls in tests target a unique per-run task name (never the real "AYAS Autonomy Observer" registration) and clean up in a `finally`.
- **Live-applied and recovery-proven on this machine, not just tested in isolation**: old shortcut removed, new one installed (Task Scheduler correctly refused → hidden-window shortcut fallback, verified via `WScript.Shell` readback: `WindowStyle Hidden` in Arguments, shortcut `WindowStyle=7`). Launched live, then the exact real-incident failure shape was reproduced on purpose — the observer's full node process tree force-killed mid-session — and **the wrapper recovered it automatically**: `daemon-state.json` heartbeat advanced 545→546, `lastObservationAt` ~31s after the kill, `daemon.lock` now owned by a fresh PID, zero manual intervention, zero new logon. `phase: PAUSED_DIRTY_REPO` is currently correct and expected (this sprint's own changes are uncommitted) — not a new defect.
- Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` PASS; ESLint `--max-warnings 0` clean on both changed `.ts` files; `git diff --check` clean; regression green — `smoke-ayas-observer-autostart` 35/35, `smoke-project-storage-hygiene` 11/11, plus re-run of `smoke-ayas-autonomy-daemon` 8/8, `smoke-ayas-daemon-authority-boundary` 23/23, `smoke-ayas-research-scheduler` 10/10, `smoke-ayas-autonomy-observer` 22/22 (none of which this sprint's changes should have touched, confirmed unaffected). Graphify: `lastAnalyzedHead` matched HEAD (`331f57a`) at sprint start, `stale: false`; not refreshed at sprint end (`.ps1` files are outside Graphify's TS/JS extraction scope, `.ts` test-file edits are additive-only within an already-graphed file); refreshed to `4e3c2f4` at the start of M26.

## AYAS M24 — EXTERNAL RESEARCH INTELLIGENCE + SOURCE RESILIENCE — 4 FAILING SOURCES ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED — 14 → 53 SOURCES — 2026-09-18

- **Closes the backlog item M23 disclosed.** The four persistently failing sources (`llama-index`, `transformers`, `openshot`, `nodejs`, each `status: ERROR` / `consecutiveFailures: 3` / `AYAS_FETCH_NETWORK_ERROR: response stream error`) were **not** a network, DNS, TLS, redirect, compression or feed-format problem. All four were reachable and returning valid Atom the whole time.
- **Proven root cause — one transport-layer defect, not four unrelated faults.** In `AyasSafePublicFetch.performOneRequest`, exceeding `maxBodyBytes` set `truncated = true` and called `req.destroy()` **before anything resolved**. Destroying a live request aborts the response stream, so `res` emitted `'error'` instead of `'end'`, and the `res.on("error")` handler won the race and resolved the generic `AYAS_FETCH_NETWORK_ERROR: "response stream error"`. The intended `AYAS_FETCH_BODY_TOO_LARGE` verdict was unreachable in practice. Reproduced deterministically offline against a `127.0.0.1` fixture before any fix was written.
- **Why exactly those four, and why the existing test missed it.** Measured live: `llama-index` 672 KB, `nodejs` 816 KB, `transformers` 1298 KB, `openshot` 1337 KB — the only four of the fourteen above the LIGHT scan's 500 KB bound; the other ten were 5–209 KB and never tripped it. The pre-existing oversize scenario used a **10 KB** body sent in one `res.end()`: the whole body lands before the destroy takes effect, so `'end'` still fires and the assertion passed against broken code. Only a body spanning multiple TCP reads reproduces it — the new suite uses one.
- **The real fix is two-part, because misreporting was only half the problem.** (1) The size bound now settles the outcome **before** `req.destroy()`, behind a first-settle-wins guard, so the verdict is deterministic regardless of which event fires. (2) A large official feed is not an error: `acceptTruncatedBody` (opt-in) returns the bounded PREFIX with `truncated: true` instead of failing. The size guarantee is unchanged — never more than `maxBodyBytes` is read, and the connection is still cut at the bound. LIGHT needs only a change signal and DEEP reads only the first N entries, and a newest-first feed puts both at the very start of the body, so a prefix answers the question exactly as well as the whole body. Refusing these feeds would have kept AYAS permanently blind to four of the most active projects it watches.
- **Resilience added to the canonical fetch layer** (`AyasSafePublicFetch` remains the only module making outbound requests; the SSRF/DNS-rebinding boundary is untouched): a failure taxonomy (`TRANSIENT` / `RATE_LIMIT` / `PERMANENT_ENDPOINT` / `UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT` / `POLICY`, defaulting to non-retryable for an unknown code), bounded retries with exponential backoff + **full jitter** for `TRANSIENT` only (default 0, hard cap `AYAS_SAFE_FETCH_MAX_RETRIES_CAP = 3`), a distinct `AYAS_FETCH_RATE_LIMITED` class recognising both 429 and GitHub's 403 + `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`, and `Retry-After` parsed and **honored** rather than overridden. A rate limit is deliberately never retried inline — a provider's reset window is minutes-to-hours, so a same-scan retry would be exactly the open-ended crawling the research policy forbids.
- **Repeated failure is now evidence, not an overwritten field.** `AyasResearchSourceCheckState` gained optional `lastFailureClass`, `lastSuccessAt`, `lastReadTruncated`, `retryAfterMs` (all optional, so existing production state stays readable under the same `schemaVersion` — no migration). New read-only `AyasResearchSourceHealth.ts` reports `HEALTHY | DEGRADED | FAILED | NEVER_CHECKED` with safe reason codes that never carry raw transport detail (pinned by test: a blocked private IP never appears in a health entry). A "transient" error recurring past the source's own threshold is reported `FAILED` — it has stopped being transient in any sense the owner cares about.
- **Source registry 14 → 53, every entry live-validated before being added** (HTTP 200, parseable Atom, ≥1 extractable entry). Two plausible candidates were **rejected rather than listed**: a TTS project whose feed is real but carries zero releases, and FFmpeg's `tags.atom` (identical content to its `releases.atom`). New coverage spans coding agents, MCP/tool use, orchestration, retrieval, memory/vector stores, evaluation, agent safety/guardrails, local inference, image/video generation, FFmpeg + the media-editing ecosystem, animation/motion (incl. Remotion — the closest existing analogue to Atölye's own code-driven video), transcription, audio/music, YouTube-side tooling, and the platform dependencies this project actually ships on (Next.js, TypeScript, React, Tailwind, ESLint, ONNX Runtime, Transformers.js, workers-sdk). Categories covered: 22. The four previously-failing sources are **kept** — removing a source is not a fix for failing to read it (pinned by test).
- **Registry entries now carry their own acquisition contract**: canonical id, provider, category, URL, acquisition method, expected content types, relevance rationale, and a per-source `policy` (rate floor, LIGHT/DEEP size bounds, retry count, failure threshold) resolved through `resolveAyasResearchSourcePolicy`. Declarative registry data, so an unusual source never means branching in the scheduler or fetch layer. A per-source `minCheckIntervalMs` floor (default 1h, well under the 6h LIGHT cadence) means a lost or corrupt scheduler state can never become back-to-back polling of someone else's endpoint.
- **Research intelligence — findings are no longer all equal.** New `AyasResearchDisposition.ts` classifies `INFORMATIONAL | WATCH | POTENTIAL_IMPROVEMENT | ACTIONABLE_PROPOSAL_CANDIDATE`, computed **deterministically** from already-structured, already-corroborated facts (taxonomy category, post-corroboration gap status, confidence, licence/cost, official-source flag, prior evaluation) — never from the external text, and never as a free-text verdict the model could inflate. The model describes; the module decides. The strongest output is a **candidate**: it authorises nothing and still enters the unchanged discovery → proposal → safety classification → owner approval → GuardedPublication path. Exactly one tier can enter discovery (pinned by test).
- **Durable novelty memory** (`AyasResearchNoveltyStore.ts`, `data/brain/self-improvement/research-novelty/`, same one-file-per-record + atomic temp/fsync/rename convention as the rest): remembers the ITEM — normalized URL, version tag, content fingerprint, first/last seen, times seen, last disposition — independently of whether it became a finding. The old dedup compared `sourceUrl` against recorded findings only, so an entry judged *not noteworthy* left no trace and was re-fetched and re-prompted on **every** scan forever. Novelty is now checked **before** the model call. A genuinely new version or an in-place edit reopens evaluation; cosmetic churn (tracking params, fragments, trailing slash, whitespace, casing) does not.
- **Prompt-injection hole found and closed.** Feed text was interpolated into the deep-analysis prompt raw, so an entry containing the literal `</UNTRUSTED_EXTERNAL_CONTENT>` would have **closed the fence early** and had everything after it read as AYAS's own instructions. A public release feed is attacker-influenceable by anyone who can publish a release, so this was not theoretical. `neutralizeAyasUntrustedText` now defangs the marker in any casing/spacing, flattens line structure (so injected text cannot forge the prompt's own `Provider:`/`Title:` lines), and bounds each field. Neutralization is lossy-but-**visible** — the attempt becomes a labelled placeholder rather than vanishing, so an injection attempt is still analysable.
- **Authority boundaries pinned by test, not asserted in prose**: all ten research modules are checked to import nothing from the approval, execution, mutation, patch or git layers (`AyasProposalApprovalService`, `AyasMicroBatchApprovalService`, `AyasAutonomousExecutionGate`, `AyasApprovalInboxStore`, `AyasGuardedPublication`, `AyasMutationScope`, `AyasMutationRegistry`, `AyasBoundedFileWrite`, `AyasPatchArtifact`, `node:child_process`, `simple-git`). The research scheduler still runs under its own gate root (`self-improvement/research`), never Package C's execution root.
- **Cadence deliberately unchanged**: LIGHT 6h / DEEP 24h, pinned by test. More coverage is never a reason to poll harder.
- **Tests**: 2 new suites — `smoke-ayas-research-source-resilience.ts` (24 scenarios: the oversize regression both ways, stream interruption, timeout, transient-retry recovery, no-retry-on-permanent, rate limit incl. GitHub's 403 form, retry cap, redirect, malformed feed, per-source isolation, failure counters, recovery reset, rate floor, health verdicts, reason-code safety, legacy-record tolerance, registry contract integrity) and `smoke-ayas-research-intelligence.ts` (28 scenarios: all disposition tiers, novelty/dedup/version/edit/churn, corrupt-record tolerance, fence-escape and variant-spelling injection, forged-field injection, schema fail-closed, authority-boundary and cadence pins). Regression green — **20 suites, 285 scenarios**, all offline/deterministic with local fixtures.
- **Live source-health validation** (bounded, isolated temp state root, LIGHT path only so no model call and no finding can be produced): **53/53 HEALTHY**. `llama-index` now reads in full under the new 750 KB default; `transformers`, `openshot` and `nodejs` read as healthy bounded prefixes (`OK_TRUNCATED_PREFIX`).
- **Production untouched**: the 14 live per-source state records, their timestamps and the scheduler's `nextLightAt`/`nextDeepAt` are byte-for-byte as they were at sprint start; no research cycle was forced, no finding recorded, no proposal created, approved or executed. One test-created novelty record (from the `example.test` fixture) was detected and removed, and the deep-research suite was fixed to inject a temp novelty store so no scenario can ever write to the real novelty root.
- Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` PASS; ESLint `--max-warnings 0` clean on all 14 changed/new files; `git diff --check` clean; Graphify refreshed at HEAD before work (13,339 nodes / 39,358 edges / 300 communities, `stale: false`, no structural anomaly).
- **Known limitation, re-confirmed for the third sprint running**: `graphify affected` is documented in `CLAUDE.md` but is still not a command in the installed CLI. Reverse-dependency evidence came from **`graphify review-delta`**, which *is* available and produced proper blast-radius output (6 changed files → 61 changed nodes → 13 impacted files, all inside the research subsystem plus the unchanged `AIProvider`/`AyasExternalResearchStore` interfaces) — a better substitute than the `query` + `grep` used in M22/M23. **Worth updating `CLAUDE.md` to point at `review-delta`.**
- **Pre-existing failure, disclosed not fixed**: `scripts/smoke-sprint-129-7-research-structured-output.ts` fails with "Production acceptance policy validation failed." This was verified to fail **identically on a clean stashed HEAD** and is unrelated to this sprint (it concerns the `src/lib/ai/` pipeline research step, not the AYAS brain research layer).

## AYAS M23 — PRODUCTION SELF-IMPROVEMENT MODE ACTIVATED — SILENT AUTOSTART DEFECT FIXED — COMMITTED / PUSHED — 2026-09-18

- **The activation exposed a real, silent defect in the canonical autostart path.** The Startup shortcut (`AYAS Autonomy Observer.lnk`, registered 2026-09-15, target `scripts/ayas-autonomy-daemon.ps1 -Continuous`) had been present and correctly configured the whole time, yet **no observer had run since 2026-09-18T00:05 local** — `daemon-state.json` was frozen at `PAUSED_DIRTY_REPO` / `heartbeatCount 503`, and `daemon.lock` still named dead PID `5932`. Running the shortcut's exact command reproduced it every time: it printed a `cmd.exe` banner and exited **0**.
- **Root cause (`7df6a00`), established from npm's own shim source, not guessed**: the wrapper built its npx argument list in `$args` — a PowerShell **automatic** variable — and splatted `@args`. On Windows `npx` resolves to npm's `npx.ps1`, which, when invoked from a script, deliberately ignores the arguments PowerShell bound for it: it re-parses the caller's raw `$MyInvocation.Statement`, drops the command name, and re-runs the remainder through `Invoke-Expression`. The caller's literal `@args` token is therefore re-evaluated **inside Invoke-Expression's own new scope**, where the automatic `$args` exists but is empty — so it splatted nothing and `npx` ran bare. A bare `npx` opens an interactive shell that immediately reads EOF and exits 0, so the wrapper's `$LASTEXITCODE` guard saw *success* while no observer had started. Renaming to `$daemonArgs` fixes it: a non-automatic name is not shadowed, so PowerShell's dynamic scoping resolves it to the wrapper's own array. The fix is three lines; no other script in `scripts/*.ps1` assigns `$args`.
- **Why the existing smoke suite missed it, and what changed**: `smoke-ayas-observer-autostart.ts` asserted the wrapper's **source text** (`/if \(\$Continuous\) \{ \$args \+= "--continuous" \}/`) — the source read correctly while the real invocation forwarded nothing. Added two scenarios (27 → 29): a guard against assigning to the reserved `$args`, and a **behavioral** test that runs the real wrapper against a PATH-shimmed `npx` reproducing npm's re-parse/`Invoke-Expression` dispatch. A first attempt at that shim simply read its own bound `$args` and passed on the broken wrapper too — useless; it was rewritten to mirror npm's dispatch exactly, then **negative-verified**: it forwards `''` (fails) on the pre-fix wrapper and `tsx scripts/ayas-autonomy-daemon.ts --continuous --interval-ms 12345` (passes) on the fixed one.
- **Canonical mechanisms used throughout; nothing was hand-edited.** The dead-PID-5932 lock was reclaimed by `acquireAyasObserverLock`'s own M12 confirmed-dead path (never deleted by hand); the stale `PAUSED_DIRTY_REPO` state was reconciled by a real observer tick (never hand-edited JSON); no new scheduled task, cron or replacement daemon was invented — the existing Startup shortcut plus `ayas-autonomy-daemon.ps1` remain the only autostart mechanism, now actually functional.
- **Live result**: observer alive and continuous (`--interval-ms 300000`), lock owned by PID `32084` with `processStartEpochMs` matching the live process **exactly (delta 0ms)**; `phase: OBSERVING`, `repoClean: true`, `graphifyFresh: true`, head `7df6a00`, `gaps: 0`. Continuity proven across **two** real ticks (`heartbeatCount` 505 → 506), not just startup. Full loop confirmed in organic cycles: observe → discovery daemon → staleness reconciliation → discovery → owner review → micro-batch accumulation → research scheduler tick.
- **Research scheduler ACTIVE and durable**: cadence intact (LIGHT 6h / DEEP 24h), `consecutiveFailures: 0`, next LIGHT `2026-09-18T17:07:53Z`, next DEEP `2026-09-19T11:07:53Z`, last successful research `2026-09-18T11:07:53Z`, 33 external-research findings on disk, 14 registered sources. No research cycle fell due during activation (`NONE_DUE` on both ticks), so none was forced.
- **Disclosed, not fixed (outside this sprint's scope)**: **4 of 14 research sources are persistently failing** — `llama-index`, `transformers`, `openshot`, `nodejs`, each `status: ERROR`, `consecutiveFailures: 3`, `AYAS_FETCH_NETWORK_ERROR: response stream error`. The other 10 are healthy (4 OK / 6 UNCHANGED), and all 14 are GitHub `releases.atom` on the same host, so this is not a blocked-host or DNS problem. Per-source failure is soft by design (Part B: "internet failure must not stop AYAS"), so scheduler-level `consecutiveFailures` is correctly 0 and research remains operational — but these four have contributed nothing for 3 consecutive cycles. **Backlog item: diagnose the `response stream error` for these four feeds.**
- **Policy verified unchanged, in source**: `AYAS_PUBLISHABLE_RUNTIME_IMPACT_CLASSES` is frozen to exactly `["TEST_ONLY", "SOURCE_ONLY"]`; `RUNTIME_CONFIG`/`SCHEDULER`/`SERVICE_RUNTIME`/`AUTHORITY_OR_STORAGE`/`UNKNOWN` remain fail-closed. Owner approval is mandatory (`decideAyasOwnerApproval` requires an explicit `APPROVE`/`REJECT`); **no auto-approval capability exists anywhere in the codebase** (repo-wide search for `autoApprove`/`auto_approve`/`automaticApproval`/`selfApprove` returns nothing). Both owner-approved lanes — `AyasProposalApprovalService` and `AyasMicroBatchApprovalService` — funnel through `runGuardedAyasPublication` → `runAyasControlledOperation`; both `AyasGuardedPublication` and `AyasRuntimeStabilityGuard` are compiled into the served bundle (29 `.next/server` chunks each).
- **Production untouched during activation**: approval inbox unchanged (25 proposals — STALE 17 / ABANDONED 1 / COMPLETED 7; **zero** PENDING/APPROVED/RESERVED/EXECUTING), 7 results, revision 80. **No proposal was approved or executed.** One micro-batch accrued organically per HEAD and was correctly left `ACCUMULATING` — never approved, never executed. **Do not expect a stable batch id here**: an `ACCUMULATING` batch is bound to its `baseHead`, so every commit canonically reconciles it to `STALE` and the next tick accumulates a fresh one at the new HEAD. That happened twice during this sprint's own two commits (`82569cda` at `7df6a00b` → `STALE`; **current: `ayas-micro-batch-a592e173-a3c5-4cfa-8c4e-54687668c707`, 1 item, `baseHead adaba9d1`**). Each batch held exactly 1 item and no tick manufactured extra work. No canary was created — the first organically generated, owner-approved TEST_ONLY/SOURCE_ONLY proposal will serve as the real live Guard canary.
- **Bundle currency**: the fix touches only `scripts/` (standalone tsx/ps1 entry points), which is not part of the Next build — `git diff --name-only f974852 7df6a00` returns no `app/` or `src/` path — so the running `.next` bundle remains current for HEAD. **No rebuild and no `:3000` restart were required or performed**; `:3000` stayed PID `20972` / HTTP 200 throughout. `/brain` correctly returns 307 → `/login` with `x-ayas-access-gate: enforced`; the authenticated Gelişim Merkezi UI was **not** rendered (no credentials — the access gate was deliberately not bypassed). Owner visibility was instead confirmed against the read-only loaders the UI reads from: micro-batch view `connected` with the active batch `ACCUMULATING` (1 item); approval inbox view `connected`, `pending 0`; owner recommendations empty; research-engine status `connected` with full per-source detail.
- Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` PASS; ESLint clean on the changed file (`--max-warnings=0`); `git diff --check` clean; Graphify refreshed to `7df6a00` (`stale: false`, 13,337 nodes / 39,354 edges / 300 communities). Regression green — 10 suites, 176 scenarios: observer-autostart 29, autonomy-daemon 8, autonomy-observer 22, daemon-authority-boundary 23, error-code-contract-observer-lock 4, research-scheduler 10, runtime-stability-guard 30, owner-approval-daemon-integration 5, autonomy-approval 29, execution-gate 16.
- **Known limitation, re-confirmed**: `graphify affected` is documented in `CLAUDE.md` but still is not a command in the installed CLI — reverse-dependency evidence came from `graphify query` plus `grep` over `scripts/`, exactly as in M22.

## AYAS M22 — RUNTIME STABILITY GUARD WIRED INTO THE REAL EXECUTION PIPELINE — COMMITTED / PUSHED — 2026-09-18

- **The gap this sprint closed**: commit `2c7a4ac` added `AyasRuntimeStabilityGuard` and its Parts A–G, but nothing in the real mutation lifecycle called them. The successful proposal execution that produced `4d848c6` proved it — a proposal reached `COMPLETED` (approved → executed → tested → committed → pushed) while leaving behind **no** stability transaction, snapshot or health decision. Graphify confirmed the guard's only inbound edges were from its own smoke suite. The guard was a library callers *may* use, so "we checked stability" was unfalsifiable.
- **Canonical integration point, chosen from Graphify evidence, not filenames**: `AyasProposalApprovalService.publishAyasApprovedProposal` — the single private function that BOTH owner-approval entrypoints funnel through (`approveAndExecuteAyasProposal`, used by `app/brain/actions.ts`'s ONAYLA VE UYGULA and by `AyasAutonomousExecutionGate.decideAyasOwnerApproval`; and `publishAlreadyOwnerApprovedAyasProposal`, used by `AyasOwnerApprovalResume`). Wiring there — and only there — makes a guarded publication the only kind this lane can perform.
- **One primitive, two lanes**: `src/lib/brain/autonomy/AyasGuardedPublication.ts` (`runGuardedAyasPublication`) is the single guarded-publication boundary. Both `AyasProposalApprovalService` (individual) and `AyasMicroBatchApprovalService` (M18.1 batch) hand it their **unmodified** publish pipeline as an opaque callback, so the two owner-approved lanes cannot drift apart. The micro-batch lane was wired in the same sprint because the architectural requirement — no owner-approved AYAS mutation reaches Git without a guard decision — is not satisfied by covering only one of two lanes.
- **Impact classification model**: `src/lib/brain/autonomy/AyasProposalRuntimeImpact.ts` classifies `TEST_ONLY | SOURCE_ONLY | RUNTIME_CONFIG | SCHEDULER | SERVICE_RUNTIME | AUTHORITY_OR_STORAGE | UNKNOWN`, derived **only** from `exactFiles` (already bound into `proposalHash`/`batchHash`) — never from free-text owner-facing prose, which is exactly the text-pattern heuristic `AyasProposalImpact.ts` was created to replace. Fail-closed three ways: the rule table is ordered most-restrictive-first with first-match-wins per file; an unrecognised/absolute/traversing/empty path is `UNKNOWN`; the combined class is the MAXIMUM severity across files, and an empty file list is `UNKNOWN`, not "harmless". Only `TEST_ONLY`/`SOURCE_ONLY` are publishable — a heavier class is refused **before any decision is minted**, so a proposal this lane can never publish never acquires a durable APPROVE.
- **No silent bypass, but a lightweight scope**: even a `TEST_ONLY` publication writes a durable transaction recording the impact class, the declared dimensions, before/after snapshots, zero violations, zero health failures, and the full `PREPARED → APPLYING → VERIFYING → COMPLETED` history. The heavy checks a source-only change rules out are recorded as an explicit `notApplicable` list on the scope (service restart, runtime-config reload, process-identity fingerprint) — a check that correctly did not run is a reviewable claim, never an invisible absence.
- **Scope decisions, with their reasons**: allowed dimensions are `source`, `git-history`, `proposal-state` and `research-scheduler`; `allowedPorts` is empty. `service`, `runtime-config` and `runtime-root` are deliberately undeclared, so any observed movement is a violation — that is what turns ":3000 was never touched" into a checked property rather than a claim. `research-scheduler` IS allowed because the scheduler is an independent concurrent actor whose cadence legitimately advances mid-publication; it is protected by a health check instead (state not lost, no new failures), which catches a real disturbance without rolling back sound publications at random. That health check activates only when a cadence was present beforehand.
- **Composition, not a second engine**: the guard performs **no** Git mutation. Its `rollback` hook only VERIFIES that each lane's own pre-commit recovery (`git reset` + `revertToHead`) restored the baseline, and escalates to `RECOVERY_REQUIRED` when it cannot prove that. A failed probe never justifies rewriting a real commit. Source inspection is pinned by test: the module's only git invocations are `rev-parse HEAD` and `status --porcelain`, and it contains no `.decide(`, no `process.kill`/`SIGTERM`, and no `reset`/`revert`/`checkout`/`--force`/`--hard`.
- **Authority ordering preserved deliberately**: HEAD-drift/staleness stays Package C's own execution-time authority (`reconcileAyasStaleProposals` + the daemon's stale-head guard), reported at the `EXECUTION` stage exactly as before. Re-checking it in the guard would have created a second, divergent definition of "stale" reporting the same condition under a different code depending on which check ran first.
- **Guard/execution-journal reconciliation, fail-closed in both directions**: before a publication may start, neither durable record may show anything in flight for that subject — no non-terminal or `RECOVERY_REQUIRED` stability transaction, and no execution journal entry classifying as `RESERVED_ONLY`/`PRE_MUTATION_GATE`/`MUTATION_UNCERTAIN`/`MUTATION_COMPLETED_UNFINALIZED`/`RECOVERY_REQUIRED`. An unreadable ledger is itself a refusal, never "no history". This catches the one window where the two records could diverge: a crash between the journal write and the guard's own transition.
- **Real defect found and fixed by the wiring**: `AyasRuntimeStabilitySnapshot`'s salt defaults to a fresh random value **per capture**, while its documented contract is that fingerprints are comparable within one guard run. The guard's own suite pinned a fixed salt and so never surfaced it; the first real integration did immediately — every tracked env var and command line appeared to "change" between before/after, turning a clean publication into a `runtime-config` out-of-scope violation. Fixed in `AyasRuntimeStabilityGuard.runAyasControlledOperation` by pinning one salt per run, making the contract true by construction for every caller.
- **Two small additive changes to already-audited modules**: `AyasRuntimeImpactScope` gains optional `impactClass` + `notApplicable` (persisted onto the transaction, purely descriptive — neither widens nor narrows what a scope permits), set via an optional 4th argument to `declareAyasRuntimeImpactScope`; `AyasRuntimeStabilitySnapshotDeps` gains optional `probeCommandLine` (default `true`), which skips process-identity fingerprinting **and its gap** for an impact class that can never restart a service — recording a gap for a correctly-skipped check would fail-close every such operation for no safety gain.
- **Tests**: `scripts/smoke-ayas-guarded-publication.ts` (32 scenarios, new) — integration-level against a real temp Git repo + real bare remote, covering the classification model, a full isolated end-to-end owner-approved publication asserted step by step (approval → guard PREPARED → mutation → tests → commit → push → guard COMPLETED → result recorded), no-restart proof, scheduler non-disturbance, gate/owner-approval invariants, every fail-closed refusal, ROLLED_BACK vs RECOVERY_REQUIRED escalation, commit/push failure handling, duplicate-resume, deterministic crash recovery, and guard/journal reconciliation. The micro-batch lane gained 2 guard scenarios in its own suite. `scripts/ayas-isolated-stability-guard.ts` (new, test-only) isolates the guard's observations in existing suites so no regression's verdict can depend on live scheduler state or the real :3000.
- Regression green: **18 suites, 339 scenarios** (runtime-stability-guard 30, guarded-publication 32, proposal-approval-service 15, micro-batch-approval-service 13, owner-approval-resume 2, autonomous-execution-gate 26, daemon-authority-boundary 23, crash-injection 6, proposal-execution-service 29, execution-journal 24, micro-batch-authority-firewall 10, patch-artifact-execution-integration 9, owner-approval-daemon-integration 5, execution-authority 29, execution-revalidation-scope-recovery 30, deep-research-engine 13, approval-durable-state-compatibility 24, proposal-terminal-state-dedup 19). `npx tsc --noEmit` PASS; ESLint 0 errors / 0 new warnings (22 pre-existing, all in `src/lib/runtime/backup/`, `src/lib/production/ProductionCompletedStageRegeneration*` and unrelated scripts); `git diff --check` clean.
- **Production untouched**: no real proposal was approved or executed (approval inbox unchanged at STALE 17 / ABANDONED 1 / COMPLETED 6, zero PENDING, zero APPROVED; `ayas-proposal-c6b7e1ff-1a50-4b39-a3dd-94177cfdc15a` still `COMPLETED`), `data/brain/self-improvement/stability/` does not exist, `.env.local` untouched, research scheduler state untouched (cadence intact, 0 consecutive failures, no run in flight), :3000 still PID 15844 / HTTP 200 throughout.
- **Known limitation, disclosed**: `graphify affected` is documented in `CLAUDE.md` but is not a command in the installed CLI (v0.17.1) — reverse-dependency evidence for the regression set was derived from `graphify explain` plus `grep` over `scripts/` instead.

## AYAS M16 — SECOND REAL SELF-IMPROVEMENT — COMMITTED / PUSHED / LIVE-VERIFIED — 2026-09-16

- **Second real mutation through the full governed loop**: proposal `ayas-proposal-57051cd1-2551-4532-adab-71882d9129ae` (mutationKind `second-safe-smoke-coverage-v1`, exactFiles `scripts/smoke-ayas-machine-health-non-gpu-stage.ts`) → execution `ayas-exec-e7d32b01-2ccf-4cbd-afd6-6f12c8130069` → result `ayas-result-ayas-proposal-57051cd1-2551-4532-adab-71882d9129ae-1789555639293` → `COMPLETED`/`EXECUTED`. This is the first execution to carry real validator evidence — durable `testResults: ["PASS"]` — closing the exact gap M15.1 flagged as a backlog item (its own first execution recorded `testResults: []`).
- **Root-caused and fixed a real observer bug, found live, not simulated**: the continuously-ticking discovery daemon (`ayas-autonomy-daemon.ts --continuous --interval-ms 300000`) minted a brand-new proposal on every 5-minute tick for the same `second-safe-smoke-coverage-v1` candidate, because `proposalHash` included `createdAt`/`lastUpdatedAt` — both stamped with the discovering tick's own timestamp — so terminal-status dedup could never recognize two ticks of the identical candidate as the same proposal. Produced 4 duplicate `PENDING` proposals before being caught. Fixed in `AyasApprovalInboxStore.proposalHash` by excluding both volatile fields from the hash material (`032dfb3`). Once the fix landed and HEAD moved past their `baseHead`, the existing stale-reconciliation mechanism automatically, correctly transitioned all 4 duplicates plus one earlier stale proposal to `STALE` — 5 `STALE` total for this mutationKind, none execution-eligible, no authorization transfer, backend-authoritative (`reconcileAyasStaleProposals` runs before every execution attempt, independent of UI state).
- **Validator binding traced end-to-end from source**: `AyasProposalExecutionService` → `AyasAutonomyDaemon.executeApproved` — exactFiles scope check (throws on mismatch) → mutation apply, which runs the mutationKind's declared validators via `runAyasBoundedMutationWithValidators` → a failing validator throws *before* any result is ever recorded (explicit in `AyasMutationRegistry.ts`'s own source comment) → only on success is `inbox.recordResult(...testResults...)` written, then `inbox.finalizeApproval(..., "EXECUTED")`, then gate close. A validator-bearing execution structurally cannot become `EXECUTED` with empty validation evidence.
- **Observer proven single-instance and dedup-safe post-fix**: process topology is one `tsx` CLI wrapper + one Node execution child (the true lock owner in `daemon.lock`) — not a duplicate pair. State machine proven live: `PAUSED_DIRTY_REPO` (correct — the generated test file was uncommitted) → `OBSERVING` within one tick of the mutation commit/push landing, proposal count unchanged (still 9 total across both mutationKinds), confirming the completed target is not re-proposed. Observer authority remains proposal-only — zero approval/reservation/execution/source-mutation capability, by code structure.

## AYAS M15.1 — FIRST REAL SELF-IMPROVEMENT EXECUTION COMPLETED — 2026-09-16

- **The full governed self-improvement loop closed end to end for the first time**: human-triggered proposal (`npm run ayas:propose`) → durable `PENDING` proposal → human `ONAYLA` (real session, real click) → separate, later human `YÜRÜT` → Package C authority chain (`AyasAutonomyDaemon.executeApproved`) → reservation → isolated gate → bounded mutation → mutation-scope verification → result recording → finalization → gate close → human Git review → commit/push. Every step used the real, already-committed M15 machinery — no shortcut, no manual state edit, no bypassed check, anywhere in the chain.
- **Two safe, zero-mutation failures were hit and diagnosed before the successful run** — both real findings, not simulated:
  1. `AYAS_DAEMON_STALE_HEAD`: a proposal's `baseHead` is fixed at creation time; once real HEAD moves past it (e.g. from an unrelated commit), that exact proposal becomes permanently unexecutable and stays `APPROVED` forever (the status model has no automatic `STALE`/`ABANDONED` transition for this case — a real, disclosed gap, not patched). Recovery requires a fresh proposal on the current HEAD; the old one's authorization can never be reused or replayed (`AyasApprovalInboxStore`'s own one-shot guards enforce this).
  2. `AYAS_DAEMON_STALE_HEAD`'s sibling, `REPOSITORY_DIRTY` (self-inflicted): the isolated execution root `data/brain/self-improvement/execution/` was missing from `.gitignore`. The moment `executeApproved` wrote its own first journal entry there, the repo looked "dirty" to `AyasExecutionRevalidation`'s own cleanliness check (`git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all`), aborting the very execution that created that evidence — 100% deterministic, would have failed identically on every attempt. Fixed with one `.gitignore` line (`/data/brain/self-improvement/execution/`, narrower than the parent so it can later hold tracked docs/schema material), verified against the real preserved failure evidence and in a clean-room worktree. No Package C source changed.
  3. A real YÜRÜT-button UX bug was found and fixed in the same arc: `executeAyasApprovedProposal` used to let thrown errors cross the Server Action boundary, and the client silently swallowed them (`catch {}`) — a human clicking YÜRÜT during the stale-HEAD/dirty-repo failures saw nothing happen at all. Fixed by having the action return `{ ok, code, inbox }` instead of throwing (Next.js redacts thrown Server Action error messages in production, so even a fixed client-side catch would have shown a useless generic string) — the client now shows a scoped, human-readable error per proposal.
- **First real mutation**: proposal `ayas-proposal-08465d45-6db1-4c4c-99ac-560ef5894958` (mutationKind `first-safe-smoke-coverage-v1`, base HEAD `1781eed719e7e3c944882b20aba2554a2da2970f`) → execution `ayas-exec-da533d51-faee-4953-bebd-8b20d879762b` → result `ayas-result-ayas-proposal-08465d45-6db1-4c4c-99ac-560ef5894958-1789542205429` → `COMPLETED` / `EXECUTED`. Isolated gate: full `CLOSED→ARMED→READY→OPEN→EXECUTING→COMPLETED→READY→CLOSED` lifecycle, sequence 8, authority lock released. Historical/global gate untouched throughout this entire M15.1 arc: `CLOSED`, sequence `14`. The exact, sole mutation — `scripts/smoke-ayas-proposal-terminal-state-dedup.ts` (12/12 scenarios), proving `AyasApprovalInboxStore`'s dedup boundary correctly distinguishes actionable statuses (dedupe) from terminal ones (fresh proposal, history preserved) — was verified byte-identical to the human-reviewed source before commit, and committed/pushed separately (`4aac750054c8f8506ea97c1e0713f69afee471ff`) only after explicit human Git review. Both prior failed-attempt evidence records (journal + gate-log) remain preserved on disk, coexisting with the success.
- **Known follow-up, not fixed here**: Package C mutation entries currently record an empty `testResults` array unless the registry entry's own `run()` wires a real validator — this first entry didn't (`testsRun: ["smoke-ayas-proposal-terminal-state-dedup"], testResults: []`), so "did it pass" was confirmed by directly re-running the test post-execution and via the full regression matrix, not by an automated in-chain check. Backlog item: **mutation registry entries should declare and execute bounded validators (typecheck/lint/the-test-itself) before finalization reports success**, so `testResults` is never trivially empty for a real execution. Not addressed in this sprint — execution semantics were deliberately left untouched.
- Full regression green throughout (18+ suites, 200+ scenarios across authorization-reservation, autonomy-daemon/approval/observer, proposal-execution-service, mutation-registry, bounded-file-write, execution-revalidation/journal/gate-transition/isolated-gate-root/authority-lock/authority, development-center/status, access-gate, phone-access-health). ## AYAS M15 — GOVERNED SELF-IMPROVEMENT PROPOSAL + EXECUTION WIRING — READY FOR REVIEW (not committed) — 2026-09-16

- **Canonical control plane frozen and proven, not just declared**: `AyasApprovalInboxStore` + `AyasInboxProposal` + `AyasAutonomyDaemon` ("Package C") is the one canonical authority for durable, non-conversational self-improvement proposals. Legacy/adjacent systems classified: `AyasAutonomousLoop`/`BrainImprovementProposal` and `AyasControlledSelfImprovement` stay `DEPRECATED_PRESERVED` (untouched, zero live callers); Guided Repair stays a `SEPARATE_NON_OVERLAPPING_DOMAIN` (live, reactive, conversation-scoped, already safety-patched in the prior M15 commit). No duplicate mutation authority: exactly two functions can ever write source (Guided Repair's `applyInternal`, Package C's new registry-driven path), on structurally disjoint trigger domains.
- **Canonical proposal schema extended, not duplicated**: `AyasInboxProposal` gains one field, `mutationKind: string`, threaded through `AyasDaemonCandidate` → `AyasAutonomyDaemon.discover()` → durable storage → the read/view layers → the execution entrypoint. It participates in `proposalHash`, so a proposal can never be silently rebound to a different mutation after creation, and approval-readiness (`isAyasProposalApprovalReady` / `isAyasDevelopmentApprovalReady`, kept in lockstep) now requires it.
- **Proposal producer reused, not reinvented**: `AyasAutonomyDaemon.discover()` (existing, already tested) remains the sole producer. The only new piece is the trigger — `scripts/ayas-propose.ts` (`npm run ayas:propose`), an explicit, human-edited-and-triggered candidate literal, never an unattended scanner. It validates `exactFiles` path-safety and mutationKind registration before ever creating a durable proposal. The continuous observer (`ayas-autonomy-daemon.ts`) is untouched and remains authority-free.
- **Safe mutation binding — closed, static, server-owned**: `src/lib/brain/autonomy/AyasMutationRegistry.ts` maps a fixed `mutationKind` string to a reviewed, committed implementation — never proposal text, never `eval`/shell/dynamic `import()`, never a client-supplied callback. The registry is **intentionally empty** for M15 — every mutation must be hand-written and reviewed before any proposal can reference it. A new schema-agnostic primitive, `AyasBoundedFileWrite.ts` (hash-precondition + atomic write + rollback-on-failure, modeled on Guided Repair's own proven pattern), is available for whoever authors the first real entry. **Deliberate deviation from the original plan**: Guided Repair's own write path was *not* refactored to share this primitive — extraction risked losing its failure-path provenance behavior for a live, already safety-patched file, with no materially simpler result; not worth the risk for a refactor alone. Guided Repair keeps its existing, unchanged implementation.
- **Real execution entrypoint, session-gated in depth**: `executeAyasApprovedProposal(proposalId)` in `app/brain/actions.ts` — accepts only a proposal id, calls `requireBrainSession()` explicitly (defense in depth beyond the middleware gate, matching `decideAyasApproval`'s existing pattern), and delegates everything else to a new, fully isolated-fixture-testable service, `AyasProposalExecutionService.ts` (re-derives proposalHash/baseHead/exactFiles from a fresh durable read immediately before executing, resolves the mutation via the registry, then delegates to the existing `AyasAutonomyDaemon.executeApproved()` — reservation, journal, gate transitions, revalidation, mutation-scope verification, and finalization are unchanged, unreproduced). Isolated gate root: `data/brain/self-improvement/` (never `data/brain` — source-proven via `AyasIsolatedGateRoot`'s construction-time refusal). `data/brain/execution/gate.json` (the historical/possibly-orphaned gate) is classified `UNRESOLVED`, left completely untouched, sequence unchanged.
- **Approval and execution remain two separate human actions**: `decideAyasApproval` never calls execution (source-proven structurally, not just by convention). `YÜRÜT` is a new, separate button in Gelişim Merkezi (`AyasDevelopmentCenter.tsx`), visible only when `status === "APPROVED"`, with its own second confirmation screen (objective/benefit/exactFiles/tests/production impact/mutationKind, one-shot-consumption notice) before dispatch. `RECOVERY_REQUIRED` exposes no replay/retry control of any kind.
- **64 new/expanded test scenarios**: `smoke-ayas-bounded-file-write` (17, new), `smoke-ayas-mutation-registry` (7, new), `smoke-ayas-proposal-execution-service` (26, new, against fully isolated fixtures — temp git repo, temp inbox, temp gate root, never real `data/brain`), `smoke-ayas-development-center` (+14, YÜRÜT visibility/confirmation/RECOVERY_REQUIRED-no-replay across every status). One pre-existing structural invariant (`smoke-ayas-autonomy-approval`'s "Stage 7B files have zero import of execution authority") was deliberately, explicitly updated: `app/brain/actions.ts` is now the one legitimate exception, with a new scenario proving execution is reachable *only* through `executeAyasApprovedProposal`, never through `decideAyasApproval`.
- Full regression green: guided repair (25+8), development center (40), development status (22), autonomy approval (20), authorization reservation (21), approval durable-state compatibility (24), execution journal (24), verified gate transition (10), isolated gate root (9), execution authority lock (11), execution revalidation/scope/recovery (30), execution authority (29), autonomy daemon (8), autonomy observer (22), observer autostart (25), reasoning (45), chat stream (20), chat quality (35), tool registry (11), tool candidate resolution (34), action runtime (17), developer workflow (9/34), workflow planner (16), workflow recovery (15), workflow store (17), write action (16), controlled self-improvement (7), autonomous foundation acceptance (42), access gate (19), phone access health (13), deferred re-eligibility (26), brain-core-ui (41), intent routing (30). `npx tsc --noEmit` PASS; ESLint 0 errors / 22 pre-existing unrelated warnings / 0 new; production build PASS; `git diff --check` clean; fresh Graphify (12,227 nodes / 36,552 edges / 324 communities). AYAS public `/brain` phone access re-verified online after every rebuild/restart. ## AYAS Production Project Catalog + Resume Awareness Sprint — READY FOR REVIEW (not committed) — 2026-09-14

- **Goal**: give AYAS read-only awareness of the real Atölye production
  project history — "Kaç projem var?", "Hangi videolar tamamlandı?", "Yarım
  kalan projeler hangileri?" — from the SAME authoritative runtime already
  resolved everywhere else, never the legacy root, never double-counted.
  **Explicitly NOT this sprint**: production execution, pipeline resume, or
  any project state mutation — discover → understand → expose to AYAS only;
  activating real resume/execution is separate, future, gated work.
- **Architecture discovery, not a new parser**: reused
  `resolveRuntimeStorageContext({})` (the one authoritative root resolver),
  `ProjectReader.getProjectFolder`/`.readJSONState` (already id-or-slug-safe
  via `ProjectFolderIndex`), and `PipelineRecoveryPlanner.createResumePlan()`
  — the SAME computation `pipeline-recovery-plan` already dispatches — for
  `resumable`/`resumeCandidateStage`. No second project-discovery path.
- **Bug found and fixed before shipping**: the first design iterated
  `ProjectReader.listProjects()` and cross-matched each record's
  `project.json`-internal `id` (a UUID, assigned once at creation) against a
  separate directory listing — a migrated project's folder name does not
  always equal its `id` field, which produced a spurious SECOND "unknown"
  entry for a folder already correctly summarized (real data went from 31
  entries with duplicates down to the correct 17 after the fix). Fixed by
  iterating the real directory listing directly and reading each folder's
  OWN `project.json` by its OWN name — one-folder-equals-one-catalog-entry
  is now a structural guarantee, not a reconciled-after-the-fact property.
- **New read model + Catalog Service** (`AyasProjectCatalog.ts`, new):
  `AyasProductionProjectSummary` (status, currentStage, hasFinalVideo,
  scene/audio/visual asset counts, resumable/resumeCandidateStage, never
  guessed) + `loadAyasProjectCatalog`/`listAyasProductionProjects`/
  `getAyasProductionProject`/`findAyasProductionProjects`/
  `summarizeAyasProductionProjects`. A `project.json` that is missing or
  malformed surfaces as an explicit `status: "unknown"` entry with a note —
  never silently dropped, never fails the whole catalog. Pure read: proven
  read-only (mtime/content snapshot, unchanged after every query) and
  path-traversal-safe (`projectId`/`titleContains` cannot escape the
  runtime root) in dedicated regression scenarios.
- **New read-only action, wired through the EXISTING architecture, not
  parallel chat logic**: `list-production-projects` added to
  `AyasExecutionPolicy.ts`'s allowlist (`write:false`,
  `requiresProject:false`) and `AyasSafeExecutors.ts` (bounds returned list
  to 50). Turkish routing reuses the established AND-gated,
  word-order-independent regex pattern (`AyasComplexityRouter.ts`:
  `PROJECT_NOUN_WORDS` + count/completed/incomplete/resumable/status signal
  words, tense-distinguishing "tamamlandı" [already done] from
  "tamamlayabil-"/"devam ed-" [capability/continuation]) →
  `classifyAyasComplexity` routes to `TOOL`. Dispatch selection for the 4
  closed filter categories (all/completed/incomplete/resumable) is
  structurally deterministic (`resolveDeterministicToolCandidate` in
  `AyasChatStream.ts`), the SAME precedent as `read-project-document`/
  `inspect-source-file` — never dependent on the reasoning model naming the
  tool correctly. A named-project query with no closed filter-kind signal
  correctly falls through to the reasoning-driven path instead.
- **The "let's continue" requirement holds via TWO independent, real
  mechanisms — a live finding, not assumed**: (1) a context-free "devam et"
  ("continue") has no antecedent for the PRE-EXISTING
  `AyasReferenceResolver.ts` to resolve, so it is asked as a clarification
  question BEFORE reasoning/dispatch is ever reached — dispatch is not even
  attempted, a stronger guarantee than "the dispatch happens to be
  read-only". (2) With real prior context (e.g. after a real "yarım kalan
  projeler hangileri?" catalog turn), the resolver instead resolves "devam
  et" to that prior reply as a `continuation` referent, reasoning/dispatch
  IS reached, and it still lands on the same read-only
  `list-production-projects` action — never `resume-stage` or any
  write-shaped action. Both mechanisms verified live end to end (Scenario
  J), Execution Gate confirmed untouched throughout.
- **Deterministic validation, counted directly**: TypeScript clean; ESLint
  0 errors / 22 pre-existing warnings, all in files this sprint never
  touched (0 new — the one warning this sprint's own new file briefly
  introduced, an unused import, was fixed before closing); `git diff
  --check` clean. New `smoke-ayas-project-catalog.ts` (7 scenarios:
  authoritative-root resolution, no-double-count, completed/video-file
  detection incl. the "completed status without a real video" edge case,
  partial-project normalization reusing `PipelineRecoveryPlanner`,
  corrupt-metadata fail-soft, read-only proof, path-traversal safety).
  `smoke-ayas-tool-candidate-resolution.ts` +9 scenarios (25→34) covering
  the new catalog candidate (direct/paraphrase/resumable/"devam et" still
  read-only/unrelated/named-project-defers/ambiguous-with-a-document/
  mutating-lookalike-defers). `smoke-ayas-reasoning.ts` +3 scenarios
  (41→44): H ("Kaç projem var?" grounds on the REAL total+completed count),
  I ("Yarım kalan projeler hangileri?" grounds on the REAL correct SUBSET,
  the completed project provably excluded), J (the two-mechanism

- **Real runtime sanity check (read-only, no secrets logged)**: against the

  incomplete, 1 unknown, 12 resumable; status distribution matches the

- **Remaining, explicitly out of scope for this sprint**: activating real

  -product-wiring gap identified in an earlier closeout-audit task
